note: Post-translation corrections shared by scripts/translate_docs.py (build-time Markdown) and de.kortty.core.TranslationGlossary (runtime HTML). ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: longer terms must precede the shorter terms they contain, or 'Benutzerhandbuch' turns into 'BenutzerAnleitung'. scope: any (default) | markdown | html. match: substring (default) | exact (the whole segment, ignoring surrounding whitespace).

replacements.note: UI label ai.inputHardening.enable; the guide must quote the checkbox verbatim.
MT renders 'input hardening' inconsistently; unify on the UI label ai.inputHardening.title.
UI label settings.ai.timeout.global; the guide must name the control exactly as the AI Manager does.
A bare 'Enabled' column label reads as a verb to MT ('Ermöglicht' = 'enables'); as a settings-table label it is the adjective. Scoped to the cell so prose is untouched.
Same label in rendered HTML, where the table cell is its own segment.
Product/technology names that MT translates literally.
'Anleitung' is the product's canonical term, matching menu.help.guide in the interface strings. Without these rows a local model renders it 'Handbuch' and the app disagrees with its own menu.
Handles 'Hilfe → Manual' too, which is why no separate row for it exists: the old table carried one and it was unreachable, since this row had already removed the word 'Manual'.

replacements.note: The rows below repair the agreement that replacing 'Handbuch'/'Leitfaden' leaves behind: those are neuter and masculine, 'Anleitung' is feminine, so every article, adjective ending and possessive around it disagrees afterwards. Longest first, as the ordering invariant requires — this one also carries the possessives.
'GitHub issue' is a proper term — MT renders it as Problem/Ausgabe.
'ASCII art' is a product term. MT renders it 'ASCII-Kunst' and, for the bare heading, 'ASCII Art.-Nr' — reading as Artikelnummer, an article number.

'Reasoning' (the AI-model capability, as in 'reasoning model'/'reasoning effort') renders as 'Argumentation' — rhetorical argumentation, a different concept entirely. The app's own UI never translates this sense (settings.ai.reasoning=Reasoning:, every guide.translation.guide.reasoning.* key), so the docs must not either. Four exact-phrase rows fix the grammatical agreement MT produces when it inflects 'Argumentation' (feminine, 'die') for what should read as the neuter loanword 'Reasoning' ('das'/'dieses'); the plain compound rows below then cover every other occurrence.

Maps to the term the corpus already uses repeatedly for the same underlying concept ('chain-of-thought' -> 'Gedankenkette' elsewhere in local-models.md and release-notes.md) instead of introducing a third German rendering of the same idea.
Bare form, last: every compound above still contains this substring, so it must run after all of them or it would truncate 'Argumentationsmodell' into 'Reasoningsmodell' etc.
MT hyphenates the compound; the app's own term (and the rest of the corpus) is one word.
MT also drops the linking 's' in the compound; same target as the hyphenated variant.
MT renders 'interface strings' two ways; this is the term used everywhere else in the corpus.
